title: Ehud Barak's Island Weekend — and the Flight Ticket in Another Man's Name | Epstein Documents
author: Grok Archive Hub
description:
In December 2014, Jeffrey Epstein invited former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak and his wife Nili to his Caribbean island. The public story has always been that Barak's island visit was brief and all business. The documents tell a longer story.
"Come to Carib?" — Epstein, 2:27 AM, December 6, 2014.
Told entirely from the primary record — the Baraks' own email, Epstein's office files from the DOJ release — this video walks the full timeline: the invitation, Nili's flight proposal (American Airlines 1275 into St. Thomas, Dec 12), Epstein's same-night approval, his office asking in writing whether to book the hotel under the name "Ehud Barak" — "or do you go by something else?" — the room booked under Nili's name instead, four days hosted on St. Thomas with lunch on the island, simultaneous invitations to Larry Summers and Tom Pritzker, and the staff farewell: "Mr. Epstein truly enjoyed this weekend."
And then the anomaly: the only flight itinerary for that trip anywhere in Barak's own email names a different passenger — COHEN/RONEN MR, on the Baraks' exact flight, arriving at the exact proposed minute, First class home to Tel Aviv (PNR 7HLSOQ). "Ronen Cohen" appears nowhere else in seven years of Barak's email, or in 1.38 million released DOJ documents. This video presents both readings of that ticket — and labels them as readings. The documents are the story.

DOJ release: EFTA00356456 (Wallace/Groff St. Thomas thread), EFTA02596796 ("ehud on island for weekend"), EFTA02346686 (Summers invitation), EFTA02300238 (island flight logistics)

title: A $1.28B reporting question. We examine Epstein’s JPMorgan timeline—and the limits of the evidence.
author: Grok Archive Hub
description: Long description: Nine reports. Two very different pictures. In this episode, The Archivist follows the filing dates, reported amounts, and overlapping activity windows behind nine suspicious activity reports tied to Jeffrey Epstein’s JPMorgan accounts. Seven filings from 2002 through 2016 listed approximately $4.3 million. Two additional filings in August and September 2019 listed approximately $1.28 billion—and both reached back to activity beginning in 2003. Using an official Senate Finance Democratic staff memorandum, its original table, and Grok Archive Hub’s source-linked investigation, we examine what those dates establish and what remains unanswered. The episode also includes JPMorgan’s response and Senate staff’s recommendation for further investigation. These are reported amounts, not a unique-dollar total or proof that every transfer was criminal. A suspicious activity report is not a criminal verdict. Evidence before speculation. Follow the timeline, examine the sources, and draw conclusions the record can support. Read the investigation: https://grokarchivehub.com/investigations/jpmorgan-nine-sars-epstein
